fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.verification_plan_present: implicit — ARM IHI 0031C defines the architectural rules, the 46-bit transaction format, mandatory DP/AP register sets, sticky-error and posted-read semantics, line-reset behavior, and SWJ-DP mode-switching. Verification categories below are derived from the spec and from CMSIS-DAP / pyOCD / OpenOCD / probe-rs open-source implementations.
verification_categories_derived_from_spe: Line reset conformance — ≥ 50-cycle SWDIO=HIGH from each reachable internal state forces SW-DP Idle; subsequent IDCODE/DPIDR read returns the correct mask-fixed value.
IDCODE/DPIDR read — every fresh SoC must respond with a valid DPIDR (bit 0 = 1) on the host's first transaction post-reset.
Request packet parity — corrupted-parity Request shall be silently dropped or set WDATAERR; subsequent line reset recovers the SW-DP.
Request Start/Stop/Park enforcement — Request with Start=0, Stop=1, or Park=0 shall be ignored.
ACK code validation — verify target returns only OK=001, WAIT=010, or FAULT=100; never any other 3-bit pattern.
Data parity on read — verify the 33rd bit returned = even parity of the 32 data bits across all DP and AP read paths.
Data parity on write — verify WDATAERR set when host writes with bad data parity; verify ABORT.WDERRCLR clears it.
Turnaround conformance — default TRNCNT=0 yields 1-cycle Turnaround; verify TRNCNT can be set 1..3 yielding 2-4 cycle Turnaround.
ABORT register — DAPABORT / STKCMPCLR / STKERRCLR / WDERRCLR / ORUNERRCLR all clear their respective CTRL/STAT bits.
SELECT register — APSEL[31:24] + APBANKSEL[7:4] + DPBANKSEL[3:0] correctly route subsequent transactions.
RDBUFF — posted-read recovery returns the data of the most recent posted AP read.
CTRL/STAT sticky bits — STICKYORUN / STICKYCMP / STICKYERR / WDATAERR set on the spec-defined trigger conditions.
CSYSPWRUPREQ / CDBGPWRUPREQ — host write → target ack within implementation-defined timeout.
CDBGRSTREQ — host write → target ack → CTRL/STAT reset to power-on state.
AP IDR readback for each implemented AP — non-zero Class+Type+Designer+Revision.
MEM-AP BASE readback — Present bit + 4 KB-aligned ROM Table address.
MEM-AP TAR + DRW round-trip — write known value to RAM, read back, verify match.
MEM-AP auto-increment Single — TAR += transfer size after each DRW transfer.
MEM-AP auto-increment Packed — multiple sub-word transfers per DRW; TAR increments per sub-word.
MEM-AP 4K wrap-around — TAR auto-increment wraps within 4 KB page boundary per spec.
MEM-AP burst write + RDBUFF flush — N successive DRW writes complete cleanly; final RDBUFF returns OK.
MEM-AP burst read + RDBUFF recovery — N successive DRW reads, RDBUFF returns the final data.
WAIT retry — host can retry the same Request until ACK=OK; verify no protocol-level retry limit.
FAULT recovery — read CTRL/STAT, write ABORT clear bits, retry; verify FAULT clears.
Posted-read overrun — issue many AP reads without RDBUFF flush; verify STICKYORUN set after the overrun threshold.
SWJ-DP JTAG-to-SWD selection (0xE79E) — start in JTAG mode; switch to SWD; verify SWD IDCODE read succeeds.
SWJ-DP SWD-to-JTAG selection (0xE73C) — start in SWD mode; switch to JTAG; verify JTAG IDCODE read succeeds.
Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) — TARGETSEL with matching TPARTNO+TINSTANCE addresses the correct target; mismatch silences all.
DLPIDR readback — TINSTANCE + PROTVSN fields correct (ADIv5.2).
TARGETID readback — TPARTNO + TDESIGNER + TREVISION fields correct (ADIv5.1+).
DHCSR halt — write C_HALT=1 + DBGKEY → CPU halts (S_HALT=1 on readback).
DHCSR step — write C_STEP=1 + C_HALT=0 → CPU steps one instruction.
DCRSR + DCRDR — host can read/write any CPU register.
CoreSight ROM Table walk — host enumerates all advertised components from MEM-AP.BASE.
SWCLK frequency margin — verify ACK=OK at the spec's max SWCLK frequency under worst-case VDD-IO + temperature.
Signal integrity — verify SWDIO setup/hold met across worst-case probe cable lengths.
VDD-IO range — verify SWD ACK=OK across the SoC's full VDD-IO operating range (e.g. 1.71 V - 3.6 V).
Concurrent CPU activity — verify SWD MEM-AP access does not interfere with CPU instruction execution (unless CPU is halted).
Power-gate isolation — when system domain is gated, MEM-AP returns FAULT (STICKYERR); after CSYSPWRUPACK=1, transactions succeed.
fields.notes: ARM does not publish an official ADIv5 compliance testbench, but open-source projects (pyOCD test suite, probe-rs integration tests, OpenOCD adapter tests) plus commercial Arm DesignVerify DAP IP testbenches cover the categories above. Real-world ADIv5 SWD interoperability is verified daily by every CMSIS-DAP / J-Link / ST-Link firmware shipping against thousands of MCU variants. The most common compliance failures historically are: (1) DPIDR bit 0 not RAO, (2) SWJ-DP selection sequence mis-handling endianness, (3) MEM-AP TAR not wrapping correctly at 4 KB, and (4) posted-read off-by-one in the AP layer.
